intro: さえ picks out the one item at the extreme end of a scale and lets everything else follow from it. In a statement it is the least likely case: if even this is true, the rest obviously is (can't even write his own name). In a condition it is the smallest requirement: if only this one thing holds, the result follows (if only I had money).

skills.rule: To say even X, where X is the most extreme case, put さえ after X in place of は, が or を.
skills.explain:
さえ marks the case that is furthest from what you would expect, so the rest of the scale is implied: 自分の名前さえ書けない (he can't even write his own name, let alone anything harder). It is most common in negative sentences and with surprise: 先生さえ知らなかった (not even the teacher knew).

さえ replaces は, が and を: 水さえ飲めない, not 水をさえ. Other particles stay in front of it: 子供にさえ分かる, 日本でさえ. For a subject, でさえ is very common: 専門家でさえ間違える (even experts get it wrong).

The edge is with も and でも. 名前も書けない also means can't even write his name, but sounds lighter; さえ stresses how extreme the case is. でも tends to generalise: 子供でも分かる (any child could understand it). だけ is the opposite direction: only X, nothing more. こそ selects X as the right one, with no sense of surprise.

examples.jp: 忙[いそが]しくて、昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]{さえ}食[た]べていません。
examples.en: I've been so busy I haven't even eaten lunch.

examples.jp: 疲[つか]れて、立[た]つこと{さえ}できなかった。
examples.en: I was so tired I couldn't even stand.

examples.jp: その問題[もんだい]は先生[せんせい]で{さえ}分[わ]からなかった。
examples.en: Even the teacher couldn't work out that problem.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は家族[かぞく]に{さえ}何[なに]も言[い]わなかった。
examples.en: He didn't say anything, even to his family.

examples.jp: この辺[へん]は夏[なつ]で{さえ}夜[よる]は寒[さむ]い。
examples.en: Around here it's cold at night even in summer.

contrast.note: も can also mean even in a negative (名前も書けない), but it is the neutral choice; さえ underlines that this is the most extreme case.
でも gives an example that stands for anyone or anything: 子供でもできる (even a child, so anyone, can do it). さえ points at one surprising case.
だけ limits: 水だけ飲んだ is I drank only water. 水さえ飲めなかった is I couldn't even drink water. Opposite directions on the scale.

mistakes.bad: 水[みず]を{さえ}飲[の]めなかった。
mistakes.good: 水[みず]{さえ}飲[の]めなかった。
mistakes.note: さえ replaces を (and が and は) instead of following it.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]が{さえ}知[し]らなかった。
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]で{さえ}知[し]らなかった。
mistakes.note: Never が plus さえ. Use さえ alone or でさえ for an even-subject.

skills.tip: Can you add let alone the rest after it? Then it is the extreme case and さえ fits.

skills.rule: X さえ ...ば means if only X: X is the one condition needed for the result.
skills.explain:
In a condition, さえ shrinks the requirement to a single thing: お金さえあれば旅行できる (if only I had money, I could travel; money is all it takes). The rest of the sentence is the result that follows. It can express a wish or regret (時間さえあれば...) or a reassurance (これさえ覚えれば大丈夫).

The conditional is almost always ば, sometimes たら. The shape depends on what さえ attaches to. A noun: 薬さえ飲めば治る. A verb: masu stem plus さえ すれば, 読みさえすれば, 寝さえすれば (a する noun can also go straight in: 練習さえすれば). A て-form: て さえ いれば / くれれば, 見てさえいれば, 来てさえくれれば. An i-adjective: く さえ あれば, 安くさえあれば. A noun as predicate: で さえ あれば, 静かでさえあれば.

だけ in a condition limits the amount (これだけあれば, if I have this much). さえ says this is the only thing that matters. Avoid と and ので after さえ: the pattern is a condition with ば or たら.
patterns: [noun] で さえ あれば

examples.jp: お金[かね]{さえ}あれば、旅行[りょこう]に行[い]けるのに。
examples.en: If only I had money, I could go travelling.

examples.jp: この薬[くすり]{さえ}飲[の]めば、すぐ治[なお]りますよ。
examples.en: Just take this medicine and you'll soon be better.

examples.jp: 天気[てんき]{さえ}よければ、山[やま]に登[のぼ]ります。
examples.en: As long as the weather is good, we'll climb the mountain.

examples.jp: 毎日[まいにち]練習[れんしゅう]し{さえ}すれば、上手[じょうず]になります。
examples.en: As long as you practise every day, you'll get good.

examples.jp: あなた{さえ}よければ、明日[あした]会[あ]いましょう。
examples.en: If it's all right with you, let's meet tomorrow.

examples.jp: 場所[ばしょ]が静[しず]かで{さえ}あれば、どこでもいいです。
examples.en: Anywhere is fine, as long as it's quiet.

contrast.note: これだけあれば足りる is if I have this much, it's enough (an amount). これさえあれば is this is the only thing I need (the condition).
しか needs a negative verb: お金しかない (I have nothing but money). It cannot sit in an if-only condition.
でも with a condition means even if: 雨でも行く (I'll go even if it rains). さえ...ば means if only.

mistakes.bad: 練習[れんしゅう]する{さえ}すれば上手[じょうず]になる。
mistakes.good: 練習[れんしゅう]し{さえ}すれば上手[じょうず]になる。
mistakes.note: With a verb, さえ follows the masu stem (し, 寝, 読み) and the condition goes on すれば. 練習さえすれば is also correct.

mistakes.bad: 時間[じかん]{さえ}あるので、行[い]けます。
mistakes.good: 時間[じかん]{さえ}あれば、行[い]けます。
mistakes.note: If only is a condition, so the verb must be in ば (or たら), not a reason with ので.

skills.tip: Say all it takes is X in your head. If that fits, write X さえ and put the verb in ば.
